issues.title: 360 panorama support: Insta360 .insp/.insv + DJI GPano files, viewable in a spherical viewer
issues.body:
## Goal
Make 360-degree panoramas first-class: Insta360 native `.insp` (equirect JPEG) / `.insv` (spherical MP4) and DJI/other GPano-tagged JPEG/MP4 exports are scanned, indexed, and **viewable in-app with a spherical (drag-to-look-around) viewer** — photos and 360 videos.

Part of epic #9.

## Scope / task plan
- [ ] Accept `.insp` as image and `.insv` as video in the format lists (`t_common.rs`) so they are scanned and thumbnailed (both are standard JPEG/MP4 containers, decoded by magic bytes).
- [ ] Detect 360 at index time: extension `insp`/`insv` or GPano `equirectangular` XMP in the file header/sidecar -> `afiles.media_subtype = 'pano_360'` (no schema change; subtype column already flows to the frontend file info).
- [ ] CORS `*` on the loopback original-media server (`t_http.rs`) so the web viewer can upload textures in desktop mode; remote mode is same-origin.
- [ ] New `PanoViewer.vue`: WebGL equirectangular viewer (image texture or `<video>` texture), drag = yaw/pitch, wheel = FOV zoom; wired into `MediaViewer.vue` when `media_subtype === 'pano_360'` (both photo and video panos).
- [ ] Locale label for the `pano_360` subtype.
- [ ] Thumbnails: `.insp` via existing JPEG pipeline; giant equirect JPEGs prefer embedded/scaled decode to stay within Pi 3 RAM (server-side concern, Phase 1/2).

## Acceptance criteria
- A library containing `.insp`/`.insv` files indexes them with correct type and `pano_360` subtype.
- Opening a pano photo in the viewer shows the spherical viewer (drag to look around, wheel zoom).
- Opening a pano video plays inside the spherical viewer.
- Regular photos/videos unchanged.

issues.title: Roadmap (epic): bigfotolab-server on Pi 3 + drop-in instant browsing + reorg templates
issues.body:
## Epic — bigfotolab enhancement roadmap

Canonical plan copies live in-repo: `ROADMAP.md` and `docs/architecture/bigfotolab-server-pi3.md` (merged in #2).

### Shipped
- #1 — rename to **bigfotolab** throughout (merged).

### Guiding requirements
- Drop-in for existing libraries: no import, browsing mirrors the on-disk directory structure as-is.
- Instant fast-scroll of thumbnails (resolution pyramid 128/256/512/1024, placeholder-first, virtualized grid).
- Headless **bigfotolab-server co-located with storage on a Raspberry Pi 3** (≤2 GB RAM, 100–300 Mbps LAN): all scan/sidecar/thumbnail I/O server-local; thin LAN clients over HTTP+WS; no per-file network I/O from clients.

### Delivery phases (milestones)
- Milestone "Phase 1" → #4 transport split + headless server skeleton
- Milestone "Phase 2" → #5 media pyramid/caching/pre-warm + #8 instant fast-scroll UX (drop-in folder-mirroring grid)
- Milestone "Phase 3" → #6 multi-user auth, per-user state, delta sync, offline cache
- Milestone "Phase 4" → #7 PWA mobile shell, adaptive video, optional off-Pi AI node

### Future feature roadmap
- #3 automated library reorganization via strategy templates (built-in + user-defined), dry-run preview, sidecar-preserving moves with undo.

### Tracking & sync
- Labels: `roadmap`, `server-backend`, `ux`. Milestones: Phase 1–4 (see [milestones](https://github.com/emmanuel-a-otchere/bigfotolab/milestones)).
- Projects v2 boards are not creatable with the current token; when the additional project space is provided, this epic and issues #3–#8 will be synced to both project spaces consistently.

issues.title: UX: instant fast-scroll thumbnail grid mirroring on-disk folder structure (drop-in for existing libraries)
issues.body:
## Goal
Scrolling a large library's thumbnails must feel almost instant, and the app must reflect the library's existing directory structure without changing it - bigfotolab is drop-in ready for any already-existing library (no import, no restructure).

## Scope / task plan
- [ ] Virtualized thumbnail grid keyed by the folder tree exactly as indexed from disk (read-only mapping; never rewrites paths).
- [ ] Placeholder-first rendering: 128 px tier paints immediately, then upgrades through 256/512/1024 tiers (works in both local Tauri mode and remote server mode).
- [ ] Lazy metadata; grid ordering/sorting driven by indexed fields, not filesystem layout.
- [ ] Confirm zero-migration: opening an existing folder just works; no import dialog, no reorganization prompt.

## Acceptance criteria
- 100k+ item library scrolls smoothly; folder tree in-app == on-disk structure; thumbnails visible <100 ms from cache on warm scroll.
issues.milestone: Phase 2 - media pyramid, caching, instant fast-scroll (Pi 3 bandwidth budget)

issues.title: Phase 4: mobile staging - PWA shell, adaptive video, optional off-Pi AI node
issues.body:
## Goal
Stage mobile: any phone/tablet on the LAN gets an installable app against the Pi backend.

## Scope / task plan
- [ ] Serve the built SPA (`src-vite/dist`) at `/` with PWA manifest + service worker (offline shell + cached media); Capacitor shell later - same codebase via RemoteTransport.
- [ ] Adaptive video: default 360p/720p H.264 proxy transcode (or HLS multi-bitrate when bandwidth allows); original via Range on demand.
- [ ] Optional AI off the Pi: CLIP/face models run on a more powerful node; Pi queries it over the API and works fine with AI disabled.

## Acceptance criteria
- PWA installs from the Pi's URL on a phone and browses/smooth-scrolls the library; video starts fast at low bitrate.
issues.milestone: Phase 4 - PWA mobile shell, adaptive video, optional AI node

issues.title: Phase 3: multi-user auth, per-user state, delta sync, offline client cache
issues.body:
## Goal
Healthy, consistent multi-user access from any LAN node, with per-user organization state and graceful offline behavior.

## Scope / task plan
- [ ] Per-user bearer tokens issued by the server; LAN-only bind (or VPN/Tailscale); optional TLS via reverse proxy; library-level ACLs.
- [ ] Per-user state (ratings, favorites, culling, collections, smart albums) in per-user rows; shared read-only index (files, thumbnails); SQLite WAL + single serialized writer (scanner).
- [ ] WS delta sync: row-level changes as IDs + hashes (no full-row polling); heartbeat + reconnect with state resync.
- [ ] Client-side cache (service worker / IndexedDB) of last-synced metadata + thumbnails - extends the existing offline-album browsing to "offline from the server".
- [ ] Server-side sidecar/filesystem watcher (inotify/FSEvents/poll) so index freshness never depends on client rescans; XMP writeback stays server-side (`metadata/xmp.rs`).

## Acceptance criteria
- N users browse concurrently; ratings/favorites isolated per user; clients survive server restart and re-sync via deltas.
issues.milestone: Phase 3 - multi-user auth, per-user state, delta sync, offline cache

issues.title: Phase 2: media serving - thumbnail resolution pyramid, Range originals, caching, pre-warm (Pi 3 bandwidth budget)
issues.body:
## Goal
Make media delivery bandwidth-first so clients on a 100-300 Mbps LAN feel instant: serve a resolution pyramid, cache aggressively, and never stream originals unless asked.

## Scope / task plan
- [ ] `GET /media/thumb/{library}/{file_id}?size=128|256|512|1024` - reuse the `AThumb` cache + generation queue (`t_protocol.rs`); format negotiation (WebP/AVIF), progressive JPEG for the viewer tier.
- [ ] `GET /media/original/{id}` - generalize `t_http.rs` loopback server to LAN with token auth; Range requests for video; `ETag`/`Last-Modified` + `Cache-Control: immutable` on content-addressed thumbs.
- [ ] Pre-warm the pyramid on scan via the existing background thumb queue (permits=1 on Pi).
- [ ] Brotli/gzip on API JSON; single WS for `thumbnail_ready` and progress; paginated/virtualized queries.
- [ ] Bandwidth budget doc: bytes per scroll position per tier; video default = small proxy transcode (360p/720p H.264), original via Range on demand.

## Acceptance criteria
- Fast scroll over a 100k-item library feels instant: 128 px placeholders render <100 ms from HTTP cache, larger tiers upgrade progressively (see companion UX issue).
- Measured wire bytes per grid page within the documented budget on a Pi 3 link.
issues.milestone: Phase 2 - media pyramid, caching, instant fast-scroll (Pi 3 bandwidth budget)

issues.title: Phase 1: transport split + headless bigfotolab-server skeleton (Pi 3)
issues.body:
## Goal
Run the bigfotolab core as a headless service co-located with the photo storage (target hardware: Raspberry Pi 3, <=2 GB RAM, 100-300 Mbps LAN), serving thin clients (browser / PWA / Tauri webview) over the LAN. No media import: the server opens library folders in place.

## Scope / task plan
- [ ] Frontend: `Transport` abstraction in `src-vite/src/common/api.js` (single choke point for all `invoke`/`listen` calls) with `TauriTransport` (current local desktop mode) and `RemoteTransport` (HTTP + one WebSocket). Mode selected at startup from config (server URL + token).
- [ ] Backend: headless entrypoint (`src-tauri/src/bin/bigfotolab-server.rs` + new `t_server.rs`) reusing existing command modules; read-only command mirror as REST/JSON; `/events` WebSocket replacing `app.emit`/`listen` (`index_progress`, `thumbnail_ready`, ...).
- [ ] Per-request `library_id` context instead of global `CURRENT_LIBRARY_ID` (`with_current_library`, `t_cmds.rs:58`, becomes request-scoped).
- [ ] Server-mode config (libraries, DB dir on server-local disk via `t_storage.rs`, port, LAN-only bind, token); SQLite WAL, capped cache.
- [ ] Cross-compile `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`; release profile `opt-level="z"`, lto, strip, panic=abort; systemd unit on Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit, read-only root + overlay).

## Pi 3 constraints (design drivers)
1 GB RAM: tokio workers=2, thumbnail decode permits=1 (existing queue in `t_protocol.rs`), SQLite cache ~8 MB, mmap off, AI indexing OFF by default (ort models don't fit), RAW thumbnails via embedded previews (libraw decode only on explicit request).

## Acceptance criteria
- Server runs as one systemd service on a Pi 3; desktop local mode unchanged.
- A browser pointed at the server can list libraries / albums / files read-only via RemoteTransport.

## Refs
- Media loopback server to generalize: `src-tauri/src/t_http.rs`; thumbnails: `src-tauri/src/t_protocol.rs` (`thumb://`); sidecar/XMP reads stay server-side: `src-tauri/src/metadata/`.
issues.milestone: Phase 1 - transport split + headless bigfotolab-server skeleton

issues.title: Feature roadmap: automated library reorganization via strategy templates (built-in + user-defined)
issues.body:
## Goal (future)
Let users re-organize an existing library automatically using organization strategy templates - built-in presets plus user-defined templates.

## Scope / task plan (roadmap only - no implementation yet)
- [ ] Built-in strategy presets: by date (Y/M/D), by event, by camera/lens, RAW+JPEG pairing, duplicate consolidation, etc.
- [ ] User-defined templates: JSON/YAML schema + in-app template editor.
- [ ] Dry-run preview: full diff of proposed moves/copies before applying.
- [ ] Execution reuses existing move/copy operations so XMP sidecars and paired assets (Live Photo components, AAE, RAW+JPEG) stay together; undo support.
- [ ] Never touches originals unless the user explicitly chooses move (copy-then-verify default).

## Notes
Pairs with the folder-structure-mirroring browsing: browsing reflects disk as-is; reorganization is an explicit, previewed, optional action.
